cinematic.note: commercial / premiere flyovers only (course-premiere-flyovers); review renders keep path.* limits
cinematic.duration_note: 20 s commercial flyover (2026-11-04): a 5 s eye-level hold at the tee with the hole sign and the banner, then a 15 s flight tee to green (flight_s: the tool scales its speed profile to it) ending over the green on the pin. No orbit (orbit.degrees 0), no title card, no outro. The yaw/pitch limits still gate the path; a hole whose 15 s flight breaks them prints FAIL and the limit, and the answer is a longer flight_s for that hole in course.json rule_overrides, not a faster camera.

intro.note: eye-level hold by the hole sign (course.json paths.signs), back_m behind and side_m beside it, looking down the line; the packager's banner sits over it. No sign: the same spot behind the back tee.

cinematic.end_note: no orbit: the flight ends end_short_m short of the green centre at end_height_m, gaze settling on end_look (green centre: the camera never crosses its own look target, so no heading flip; 'pin' is the other value). 20 m / 15 m stopped visibly short of the green (Tierra 10, 11/4), 10 m / 12 m fills the frame with it. A flight averaging over fast_flight_m_s gets no bunker dips at all and follows the line (a dip at 25 m/s was 43 deg/s of yaw on Tierra 10); bunker_dip_height_fast_m is kept for a course that lowers fast_flight_m_s. end_gaze_fraction: the share of the flight over which the gaze moves from the line ahead to the green; 0.6 of a 15 s flight is 9 s, and a 40 deg swing eased over 9 s peaks near the 8 deg/s pitch limit.
cinematic.limits_note: 20 / 15 deg per s are commercial-pace limits for the 15 s flight (flyover_path.py, 11/4: all 18 Tierra holes pass at 19.1 / 14.6; the former 12 / 8 were set for a 36 s drift and fail 10 of 18 at this pace, and even a 25 s flight fails 4, 9, 17 on them). A hole that looks rushed in the render gets a longer flight_s in course.json rule_overrides, not a limit change.
cinematic.start_note: rise_ahead_m and rise_keep_offset: the first flight point sits rise_ahead_m along the line from the intro camera and keeps rise_keep_offset of the camera's sideways offset from the line, so the return from beside the sign to the line is spread over two legs (a 7 m jog in 30 m at 25 m/s was 19 deg/s of yaw). end_ease_m / end_speed_factor: the camera eases to end_speed_factor of base speed over the last end_ease_m, so the near look target does not sweep the pitch (50 deg/s at full speed on Tierra 10).

render_4k.format: png (lossless; Unity's encoder has no compression setting)
render_4k.supersample_note: render target = width*supersample, clamped to SystemInfo.maxTextureSize, bilinear downsample

motion_blur.method: accumulation across shutter/360 of the frame interval; PPv2 MotionBlur disabled during the pass

disk.on_low_space: halt the queue with DISK_SPACE_EXCEEDED (not skip)

render_4k.note: a 25 s hole is ~1,500 frames, ~18 GB; 18 holes ~300 GB; editor only (post-processing needs the editor, batch mode has none)
render_4k.crash_note: Tierra 10, 11/3: the editor died in D3DKMTOpenResource at frame 401 of 1,200 with supersample 1.5, MSAA 8 and 8 sub-frames (a 5760x3240 MSAA-8 target, ~600 MB, and 3,200 manual Camera.Render calls through the post stack). Now: supersample 1.0 with MSAA 8 plus 4 accumulated sub-frames, GL.Flush / UnloadUnusedAssets / GC every housekeeping_every_frames, and resume keeps frames already on disk so a crash costs minutes, not the hole.

banner.title: Hole #{hole}
banner.note: lower-left banner over the intro hold, as a commercial flyover card: hole number, the flyover tee's card yardage, par; sizes for 2160 px, scaled to the frame

package.frame_tolerance_note: frames may fall short of seconds x fps by up to this many at the tail (clip length rounding); any gap in the sequence still fails
